'''Robert Vince''' (born November 20, 1940) is an American scientist known for his contributions to the research in the area of drug design. He is currently the director and professor at the Center for [[Drug design|Drug Design]] at the Academic Health Center for the [[University of Minnesota]].

== Biography ==
Robert Vince was born in [[Auburn, New York|Auburn]], New York. After graduating with a Bachelor of Science in Pharmacy in 1962, Vince joined the research group of Prof Howard J. Schaeffer at [[SUNY Buffalo]] in New York, where he obtained his doctoral degree in [[medicinal chemistry]]. He subsequently joined the [[University of Mississippi]] for a brief stint as assistant professor of medicinal chemistry. In 1967, he joined the medicinal chemistry faculty at the [[University of Minnesota]].<ref name="singhvincereview">Singh, R.; Vince, R. “2-Azabicyclo[2.2.1]hept-5-en-3-one: Chemical Profile of a Versatile Synthetic Building Block and its Impact on the Development of Therapeutics" ''Chemical Reviews'' '''2012,''' ''112,'' 4642–4686.</ref> In 2002, Vince established the Center for Drug Design within the Academic Health Center of the University of Minnesota, where he continues as director and maintains his research program.<ref>{{cite web|title=About Center For Drug Design|url=http://www.cdd.umn.edu/AbouttheCenter/index.htm}}</ref>

== Career Contributions ==
As a graduate student, Vince’s research on the design of acyclonucleosides, with Howard J. Schaeffer at SUNY Buffalo became an integral part of the discovery of anti-viral drug [[acyclovir]].<ref>Howard Schaeffer, S. Bittner, Robert Vince, S. Gurwara "Novel substrate of adenosine deaminase". ''Journal of Medicinal Chemistry'' '''1971,''' ''14,'' 367–369.</ref> Later, Prof Schaeffer continued the development of [[acyclovir]] at Burroughs Welcome & Company, with pharmacologist [[Gertrude B. Elion]] who was awarded the 1988 [[Nobel Prize]] in Medicine, in part, for the development of [[acyclovir]].<ref>{{cite web|title=The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 1988|url=https://www.nobelprize.org/nobel_prizes/medicine/laureates/1988/}}</ref> Dr. Vince continued his work on [[antiviral drug]] candidates at the University of Minnesota, where he went on to develop carbocyclic nucleosides termed 'carbovirs'. This class of medicinal agents included the drug [[abacavir]].<ref>Vince, R. "A brief history of the development of Ziagen" ''Chemtracts'' '''2008,''' ''21,'' 127–134.</ref> Abacavir was commercialized by [[GlaxoSmithKline]] as [[Ziagen]] for the treatment of [[AIDS]]. Sales from Ziagen have resulted in generation of more than 600 million US dollars in royalties for the University of Minnesota.<ref name=singhvincereview />

His synthesis of [[abacavir]] made use of a bicyclic γ-lactam, 2-azabicyclo[2.2.1]hept-5-en-3-one, as a chemical precursor. In recognition of his contribution to the development of this field, [[Chemical and Engineering News]] gave this molecule a general name, ‘[[Vince lactam]]’ in 2003.<ref>Rouhi, M. ''Chem. Eng. News'' '''2003,''' ''81,'' 40.</ref> Vince lactam has since been utilized to prepare several drugs and pharmaceutical candidates.<ref name=singhvincereview />

== Recognition ==
For his work, Vince has received recognition from several avenues. He was elected as the Fellow of AAAS by [[The American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 2000.<ref name="AAASInduction">{{cite web|title=The American Association for the Advancement of Science: News and Notes October 2000|url=http://worldtracker.org/media/library/Science/Science%20Magazine/science%20magazine%201999-2000/root/data/Science%201999-2000/pdf/2000_v290_n5492/p5492_0821.pdf}}</ref> He was inducted into the Medicinal Chemistry Hall of Fame of the [[American Chemical Society]] in 2007.<ref name="ACSInduction">{{cite web |title=ACS Medicinal Chemistry Hall of Fame - Robert Vince, PhD|url=http://www.acsmedchem.org/?nd=Vince}}</ref> Vince was awarded Honorary Doctorate of Science Degree by his alma mater SUNY Buffalo,<ref name="SUNYDegree">{{cite web|title=Four to Receive SUNY Honorary Degrees at UB|url=https://www.buffalo.edu/news/releases/2010/03/11150.html}}</ref> and the prestigious Imbach Townsend Award by the International Society for Nucleosides, Nucleotides and Nucleic Acids, in 2010.<ref name="ImbachTownsend">{{cite web|title=International Society for Nucleosides, Nucleotides and Nucleic Acids 2010 Imbach Townsend Award | url=http://www.cdd.umn.edu/prod/groups/ahc/@pub/@ahc/@cdd/documents/article/ahc_article_251438.pdf}}</ref> The same year, Minnesota Inventor’s Congress inducted him into Minnesota Inventors Hall of Fame, along with Nobel laureate [[Norman Borlaug|Dr. Norman Borlaug]] (posthumously).<ref name="MNHalloffame">{{cite web|title=Dr. Robert Vince - 2010 Inductee Minnesota Inventors Hall of Fame|url=http://www.minnesotainventors.org/inductees/robert-vince.html}}</ref> In 2011, he was inducted into Minnesota Science & Technology Hall of Fame.<ref name="MNSCTechHOF">{{cite web|title=Robert Vince: How he has transformed the scene|url=https://www.msthalloffame.org/robert_vince.htm}}</ref> In 2017, the [[New York State Senate]] adopted a legislative resolution commending him upon the occasion of his designation as a 2017 Inductee into the Auburn Alumni Hall of Distinction.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/resolutions/2017/k281|title=Resolution# K281|date=2017-04-03|website=NY State Senate|language=en|access-date=2019-06-03}}</ref> He was honored at the [[National Academy of Inventors]] (NAI) Annual Conference as an NAI Fellow in 2018,<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://research.umn.edu/inquiry/post/u-inventor-robert-vince-honored-nai-fellow|title=U Inventor Robert Vince Honored as NAI Fellow|date=2018-05-29|website=Inquiry {{!}} Office of the Vice President for Research|language=en|access-date=2019-06-03}}</ref> and recently was selected for the Innovation Impact Case Award (2022).<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=hsantiag |date=2022-04-19 |title=Innovation Impact Case Award: 2022 Awardees |url=https://research.umn.edu/funding-awards/innovation-impact-case-award/2022-awardees |access-date=2022-05-04 |website=Office of the Vice President for Research |language=en}}</ref>
